conditions.label: Dissection of ascending aorta
conditions.note: acute type A, root through ascending aorta into proximal arch

reports.text: Portable AP chest. The mediastinum is widened. Lungs are clear. No pneumothorax. No pleural effusion. Bony thorax intact.

CT angiography of the chest with IV contrast, dissection protocol.
An intimal flap begins at the aortic root and extends through the ascending aorta into the proximal aortic arch. Aortic root measures 4.2 cm. The descending thoracic aorta is normal in caliber without a flap. No pericardial effusion. No mediastinal hematoma beyond the aortic wall. Lungs clear; no pleural effusion.
reports.conclusion: Acute type A aortic dissection from the aortic root into the proximal arch.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL ED -- PHYSICIAN NOTE
Arrived by ambulance 02/13/2026 09:31

Chief complaint: acute upper back pain.

HPI: 28-year-old man with Marfan syndrome and a known thoracic aortic root aneurysm, followed for aortic regurgitation since 2024 and seen here in 2025 for a lens problem in his right eye. Brought in after abrupt, severe pain between the shoulder blades that started while he was sitting at his desk. He calls it sharp and ripping.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.
PSH: dental extraction 2024.
FHx: father with Marfan, aortic root replaced at 38; paternal uncle died suddenly at 31, thought to be dissection; sister with Marfan.
Social: never smoker; rare alcohol; graduate student.

Exam: Temp 36.7 C. BP 88/40 right arm, 112/44 left arm. HR 112. Tall, thin, limbs and fingers disproportionately long. Heart: high-pitched early diastolic decrescendo murmur, loudest at the left sternal border. Lungs clear.

Course: two large-bore IVs. Portable chest film with a wide mediastinum. Cardiothoracic surgery at the tertiary center called before CT. CT angiogram: acute type A dissection from the root into the proximal arch. CBC, BMP and high-sensitivity troponin within normal limits. Aspirin held. Accepted in transfer by cardiac surgery; left by critical care transport at 13:55.

Diagnosis: acute type A aortic dissection.
Allergies: NKDA.

Emergency medicine attending

documents.title: Discharge Summary -- Cardiac Surgery
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
TERTIARY CARE CENTER -- CARDIAC SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 02/13/2026 (transfer from outside ED). Discharged 02/20/2026.

Principal diagnosis: acute type A aortic dissection.
Background: Marfan syndrome (FBN1); aortic root aneurysm 4.2 cm; chronic severe aortic regurgitation; mitral valve prolapse with mild MR; bilateral ectopia lentis.

Operation 02/13/2026: emergency valve-sparing aortic root replacement (reimplantation) with hemiarch replacement, via median sternotomy, under cardiopulmonary bypass with circulatory arrest for the hemiarch. Native aortic valve preserved. Intraoperative TEE after repair: trace aortic regurgitation, LVEF 55%.

Hospital course: extubated postoperative day 1. ICU through day 2, then step-down. Chest tubes out day 3. Pain controlled with oral acetaminophen. Ambulating independently by day 4. Uneventful recovery.

Discharge medications:
- metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily
- lisinopril 10 mg daily
- aspirin 81 mg daily (resumed)
- acetaminophen 1000 mg every 8 hours as needed for pain

Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: sternal precautions -- no lifting over 10 lb, no pushing or pulling, no driving for 6 weeks. Keep the incision clean and dry. Referral placed to outpatient cardiac rehabilitation. Cardiac surgery clinic in about 5 weeks. Primary care within 2 weeks. Call or return for fever, wound drainage, chest or back pain, or shortness of breath.

Cardiac surgery

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with pt, staying with his parents for now. Home since Friday after emergency aortic root/hemiarch repair for a type A dissection. Pain 3/10, using acetaminophen once or twice a day. Incision dry, no redness or drainage. No fever. Walking around the house several times a day. Has all 3 heart meds plus Tylenol, reviewed against discharge list -- matches. Knows sternal precautions. Parents driving him. Booked with PCP 3/3, surgery clinic letter says late March. Reviewed when to call 911.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up after aortic dissection repair

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Discharge summary and outside ED record reviewed.
2/13 sudden ripping interscapular pain at his desk; outside ED: BP 88/40 R, 112/44 L, HR 112, new early diastolic murmur, wide mediastinum on CXR; CTA type A dissection root to proximal arch. Transferred, emergency valve-sparing root reimplantation + hemiarch the same evening. TEE afterward trace AR, EF 55%. Home 2/20.

Now: dad drove him in. Sore at the sternum, acetaminophen a couple times a day. Walking 15-20 min twice daily. First cardiac rehab session was yesterday. No fever, no wound drainage, no new back or chest pain, no shortness of breath.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 10, aspirin 81, acetaminophen PRN. Matches the discharge list.

Exam: looks tired but well. BP and HR as charted -- pulse pressure normal now. Sternotomy incision intact, edges together, no erythema or drainage; sternum stable. Heart regular, I don't hear the old diastolic murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Weight down a few pounds from the hospital stay.

A/P
1. Type A aortic dissection s/p valve-sparing root + hemiarch replacement -- recovering on schedule. Updated the problem list: root aneurysm and AR marked resolved with the repair; dissection kept. Continue meds. Sternal precautions until 6 weeks. Surgery clinic 3/25.
2. Marfan syndrome / MVP / ectopia lentis -- unchanged.
3. Spent time on how he's coping -- shaken, but has family around; he knows to reach out.
See me again in about 5-6 weeks.

documents.title: Cardiac Surgery Postoperative Visit
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Cardiac surgery clinic, 03/25/2026.

Six weeks after emergency valve-sparing aortic root replacement with hemiarch for acute type A dissection. Progressing well in cardiac rehabilitation. Minimal sternal discomfort; off acetaminophen most days.

Exam: sternotomy healed, sternum stable. Regular rhythm. Lungs clear.

Plan: may advance activity per cardiac rehab and resume driving. Lifelong avoidance of heavy lifting and straining (isometric exertion). Continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, aspirin 81 mg. Surveillance CT angiogram of the chest at about 6 months after surgery; ongoing care with his cardiologist.
Allergies: NKDA.

Cardiac surgery

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
8 wk out from the type A repair. Surgery clinic 3/25: healed, cleared to drive and progress through rehab, CTA around August.

Drove himself today. Back in his own apartment. Rehab 3x/week, says he feels better than he did before the surgery -- more energy on the stairs. Not taking acetaminophen anymore. No chest or back pain, no palpitations, no swelling. Thesis defense pushed to summer, his advisor has been flexible.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 10, aspirin 81. NKDA.

Exam: well. Sternotomy well healed. RRR, soft systolic click at the apex, no diastolic murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P: s/p aortic dissection repair, doing well. BMP and CBC today. Keep cardiology and CTA in summer. Annual physical in the fall.

CT angiography of the chest with IV contrast.
Comparison: 02/13/2026.
Postoperative changes of aortic root replacement and hemiarch graft. Graft intact, without contrast leak or pseudoaneurysm. Native distal aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta normal in caliber, no residual dissection flap. Sternotomy wires intact. No pericardial or pleural effusion. Lungs clear.
reports.conclusion: Intact aortic root and hemiarch repair. No residual dissection.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP -- FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 07/16/2026

Five months after emergency valve-sparing root and hemiarch replacement for type A dissection. Finished cardiac rehab. Feels well, no chest or back pain.

CTA 7/8: repair intact, no residual dissection, distal aorta normal caliber.
Echo today: trace AR, LVEF 55%, MVP with mild MR.

Plan: continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril 10 mg and aspirin 81 mg daily. Lifelong activity restrictions as discussed. Yearly imaging of the aorta, alternating echo and CTA. Return in 12 months.
Allergies: NKDA.
